figures.finding: A minor is a person of either sex under eighteen; a minor is under a guardian for his person and represented by a tutor in his pecuniary interests, and may perform juridical acts only where the law provides.
figures.applies: Ethiopia, Civil Code arts. 198-199 (1960, in force).

sources.said: A minor is a person of either sex who has not attained the full age of eighteen years.

In matters concerning his pecuniary interests and the administration of his property, a minor shall he represented by a tutor. (3) The minor may not perform juridical acts except in the cases pro· vided by law.

figures.finding: Persons incapable under the law (minors among them) may not be traders, a tutor may not carry on a trade for a minor, and only a minor emancipated under the law may carry on a trade.
figures.applies: Ethiopia, Commercial Code 2021 arts. 10-12; the share company director's age was not found in the text read.

sources.said: Persons incapable under the relevant law may not be traders.
Tutors may not carry on a trade in the name and on behalf of a minor.
Minors emancipated in accordance with the relevant law may carry on a trade.

figures.finding: Ethiopia's Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019 forbids employing anyone under fifteen (raised from fourteen) and makes a young worker a person of fifteen to under eighteen, who may do only non-hazardous work for at most seven hours a day; the law sets no light-work age.
figures.applies: Ethiopia (Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019, in force as of 2023).

sources.said: Article 89(1) of the Labour Proclamation No.1156/2019 defines young worker as “a natural person who has attained the age of 15 but is below the age of 18 years”.
replaced with Labour Proclamation No.1156/2019, which raised the minimum age for employment from 14 years to 15 years.
work for a maximum of seven working hours per day
Though light work is not specifically established by the national legislation of Ethiopia
